subject: Production throughput variance — coordinated mitigation & customer comms
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, ops@bluegrid.energy
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Alert: sudden 99th-pct latency spike for bluegrid-prod (10/07)

Team —

We detected a sustained increase in 99th percentile token latency across bluegrid-prod between 07:45–08:05 PT (~+220ms at 99th; p50 unaffected). Throughput (tokens/s) also shows intermittent drops aligning with the latency spikes. Early indicators point to a regression in KV cache hits following the 10/06 kernel switch on the serving fleet.

Immediate ask: can engineering validate whether the kernel selector change pushed to the US-west pool is causing KV miss amplification for certain seq-length distributions? Connor, can you take lead and confirm
- which kernel change rolled at 02:30 UTC 10/06
- correlation between cache eviction events and the spike

I'm looping Marissa and Jonas for customer comms and product context. BlueGrid ops are on the To line — Tara, we saw your service degrade; we will provide status updates ASAP.

Attaching a small KV cache dump for quick triage (kv-cache-dump-20261007.txt).

-Hannah
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, ops@bluegrid.energy
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Alert: sudden 99th-pct latency spike for bluegrid-prod (10/07)

Thanks Hannah. Quick product/ops coordination checklist from my side: 
- High priority: short customer-facing note acknowledging the impact and ETA for a mitigation plan. Prefer a single message to BlueGrid to avoid confusion.
- Product ask: if this is kernel selector related, how risky is reverting vs. targeted config change on the affected US-west pool? Any perf/cost tradeoffs?
- Roadmap question: if this pattern is due to sequence-length skew on BlueGrid workloads, we should consider a short-term weight tweak in routing and add a task for KV-cache diagnostic visibility on the roadmap.

Connor/Karthik — please draft a one-paragraph engineering summary I can send to BlueGrid within 30 minutes. Tara (BlueGrid), we'll follow with a clear mitigation plan and expected timelines in the next update.

-Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, ops@bluegrid.energy
Date: 2026-10-07T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Alert: sudden 99th-pct latency spike for bluegrid-prod (10/07)

On 2026-10-07 08:12 PT Hannah Schmitt wrote:
> We detected a sustained increase in 99th percentile token latency across bluegrid-prod between 07:45–08:05 PT (~+220ms at 99th; p50 unaffected).

I pulled the host-level metrics and correlated them with the kernel selector rollout. Summary: the kernel selector v2.4 was applied to the us-west GPU pool at 02:30 UTC 10/06. After the rollout we see a small but consistent increase in KV-cache eviction rate for requests with long prefixes (>1k tokens) that BlueGrid regularly issues. Eviction rate went from ~0.6% to ~3.4% on affected nodes.

Short-term mitigation options: 
1) Pin the selector to v2.3 on the us-west pool (fast rollback, low risk) — expected to bring 99th down ~180–200ms within 5–10m after roll.
2) Apply a targeted cache window change for BlueGrid's routes (config only) — lower blast radius, expected improvement ~120–160ms, no rollback needed.
3) Route heavy long-prefix requests to a dedicated fallback model variant with larger KV windows (resource/cost impact: ~+12% token cost).

I'm attaching a draft rollback/runbook (rollout-plan-v2.pdf). Recommend option 1 for fastest customer relief while we instrument longer-term fixes. If we go with rollback, ops will need a 10-minute maintenance window to drain in-flight KV states.

I can execute option 1 now if approved.

-Connor
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: ops@bluegrid.energy, Tara Singh <tara@bluegrid.energy>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: BlueGrid: brief update on degraded performance (we're on it)

Tara / BlueGrid ops —

We identified the cause of the degradation impacting your production endpoints: a recent serving kernel selector change increased KV cache evictions for some long-prefix request patterns. Our SRE team proposes a rollback to the previous selector (v2.3) to restore expected latency quickly; this carries minimal risk and should improve 99th percentile latency by ~200ms within 10 minutes of rollback completion.

Planned next steps: 
- We are ready to initiate a targeted rollback on the us-west pool now; expected completion 10–15 minutes. During the rollback we will drain in-flight requests on affected nodes.
- Post-rollback we will monitor for 30 minutes and share a follow-up summary including metrics and a permanent mitigations plan.
- If you prefer we can instead apply a config-only routing adjustment to reduce immediate impact with lower operational touch (we can advise on tradeoffs).

Please reply with your preference or approval to proceed with the rollback. We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-08T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Post-rollback notes & next steps (BlueGrid incident SUP-2109)

Follow-up notes after rollback completed at 09:45 PT: 99th reduced ~195ms, throughput stabilized; KV eviction returned to baseline. Good work.

Action items / product asks I want tracked into next two sprints: 
- Add a per-customer KV hit-rate dashboard (high priority for strategic accounts).
- Expand selector canary gating to include seq-length distribution tests.
- Evaluate a route-level fallback policy primitive so account teams can opt-in without per-deploy changes.

Marissa/Karthik: please confirm whether we should propose a 10% goodwill credit to BlueGrid under BG-4821; I can draft the finance note if you want a recommended amount.

I'll file SUP-2109 with the above summary and link to the runbook/metrics in the incident doc.

-Jonas
Head of Product, Serving Runtime
